scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The Connection Lab records fictional paper strips for a sorting activity. Each row has an example identifier, a measured length and a checked short-or-long label. Tara notices that the length describes an input feature, while the label is the result the helper should learn to predict.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: One example appears twice. Another has no label, and the same identifier carries two conflicting measurements elsewhere. Neel wants to choose whichever value makes the table look tidy. The teacher instead asks the team to preserve the uncertainty and review the source record.
scenes.speech: One example appears twice. Another has no label, and the same identifier carries two conflicting measurements elsewhere. Neel wants to choose whichever value makes the table look tidy. The teacher instead asks the team to preserve the uncertainty and review the source record.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: A neat table can still contain poor evidence. Repeated copies do not create independent examples, and invented labels can teach mistakes. The team keeps only necessary object data, sets unresolved rows aside and documents repairs. Learners’ names and phone numbers have no role in this sorting task.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: The same example identifier has two different recorded lengths. The original measurement has not been checked. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: The same example identifier has two different recorded lengths. The original measurement has not been checked. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: What should happen to a conflicting row?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Hold the row for source review and document the correction. Guessing a convenient value would hide uncertainty rather than improve the evidence.
scenes.speech: Hold the row for source review and document the correction. Guessing a convenient value would hide uncertainty rather than improve the evidence.
scenes.dialogue: Identify duplicate, missing and conflicting records.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate features and labels, then record quality, then only necessary data. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
